Hi Samantha (and Paul),

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, I’m sharing a concise mutual action plan (attached) that aligns the evaluation milestones, technical acceptance criteria, and procurement/billing steps for the AWS private offer. The attachment (HelioZen_MAP_v2.xlsx) is organized by week and owner. High-level asks from our side:

- Confirm procurement contact and preferred PO cadence (one-time PO vs monthly/quarterly).
- Confirm target production cutover date — you mentioned early Jan; we captured 2027-01-10 as a draft start.
- Confirm whether finance wants invoices via AWS Marketplace (recommended) or direct Redwood invoice (we can accommodate but need AP contact + tax form).

Immediate next steps we propose:
1) HelioZen returns the completed MAP with any date changes (Samantha).
2) Redwood to create the AWS private offer (Seller ID and SKU mapping) and share the AWS PO template for the HelioZen procurement team to populate (Karthik + Finance).
3) Technical acceptance window starts when HelioZen completes the staged workload test (detailed checklist attached).

Attachments: HelioZen_MAP_v2.xlsx, technical-acceptance-checklist.xlsx

I’ll be the primary Redwood point-of-contact for coordination — copying Karthik for marketplace setup and Marissa for billing/finance.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Private Offer Onramp — HelioZen procurement corridor and MAP

Kimberly,

Appreciate the clear MAP. Quick read-through from procurement — this is very helpful. A few clarifications and one ask from our side:

- PO cadence: We prefer a single annual PO for 2027 with quarterly invoices if AWS Marketplace supports invoicing cadence. If AWS requires monthly invoices, we will need to align on a consolidated invoice flow.
- Billing path: Please confirm whether the private offer will route billing through AWS Marketplace (our preference) — i.e., HelioZen receives invoices from AWS and remits to AWS, or does Redwood invoice HelioZen directly? We need to confirm the cash flow for our treasury team.
- Compliance evidence: Could you attach the SOC2 report or point us to the audit kit? Treasury will ask security questions before issuing the PO.

I attached a short procurement checklist (HelioZen_Procurement_Questions.docx) with items we commonly need before legal approves.

Confirmed dates: We can aim for the suggested production start on 2027-01-10 provided the technical acceptance completes by 2026-12-20. We’ll try to expedite approvals but please mark key deliverables that must happen before that acceptance window.

Thanks,
Samantha Lee
Procurement Manager | HelioZen
samantha.lee@heliozen.com

Subject: Re: Private Offer Onramp — HelioZen procurement corridor and MAP

Samantha — quick answers and a small clarification from the marketplace setup side: 

1) Billing path: For AWS Private Offer flows we typically create an offer that routes invoicing through AWS Marketplace (HelioZen receives invoices from AWS). That keeps billing aligned with your existing AWS procurement workflows and removes the need for a separate Redwood invoice. We will confirm with the marketplace team and share the Seller ID and SKU mappings in the next update.

2) SOC2 / compliance: Kimberly — can you share the audit kit link? Marissa, I’m flagging you for the compliance docs and finance contact so we can get procurement what they need.

3) Technical acceptance: Attached is the acceptance checklist (technical-acceptance-checklist.xlsx) that maps tests to success criteria and owner. We recommend a 48-72 hour soak after your staged load to validate latency percentiles and KV cache behavior.

4) Marketplace steps (high level):
   - Redwood opens Private Offer in AWS Marketplace and proposes terms (Redwood).
   - HelioZen signs off on PO/terms and returns signed PO (HelioZen).
   - AWS activates the private offer and billing begins per AWS Marketplace cadence (typically monthly invoice).

I’ll own creating the private offer and will share the AWS_PO_Template.pdf for HelioZen finance to populate.

—Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Private Offer Onramp — HelioZen procurement corridor and MAP

Paul / Samantha — great, and thanks for the PO draft. Final confirmations below so procurement/legal can move forward: 

1) Billing path: Confirmed — we will route billing through AWS Marketplace. HelioZen will receive invoices from AWS per the marketplace cadence. Redwood will provide the Seller ID, SKU mapping, and the AWS PO template for your AP team to complete. (Karthik to send Seller ID + template by EOD Friday.)

2) Termination language: Redwood will accept standard private offer termination clauses with a 30-day wind-down for committed annual contracts. I’ve attached a short redline summary in the MPA workbook where we call out Section 5 language that usually satisfies marketplace terms. If Legal wants a different flow we can work through the specific clause but we generally avoid direct refunds outside AWS invoices.

3) Pricing confirmation: Redwood confirms the 12% Enterprise discount for Year 1 on the listed SKUs (attached). We’ll lock pricing in the private offer request.

4) Timeline (mutual action plan milestones):
   - 2026-12-03: Redwood sends Seller ID, SKU mapping, and AWS_PO_Template.pdf (Karthik).
   - 2026-12-06: HelioZen submits signed PO back to Redwood (Paul).
   - 2026-12-10: Redwood creates Private Offer in AWS and initiates activation.
   - 2026-12-20: Completion of technical acceptance (staged load + soak).
   - 2027-01-10: Target production cutover / billing starts.

5) Compliance: Marissa will share SOC2 summary and audit kit link separately (cc’d).

6) DocuSign / signature: We’ll also prepare a DocuSign request for the commercial exhibit and MPA; link will be sent once PO and private offer terms align.

Next steps: Karthik will send the marketplace artifacts today; Marissa will post the SOC2 link to the Drive folder and I’ll upload the signed MAP version to our shared Drive. Once the PO is in hand we’ll start the AWS activation.

Thanks everyone — looking forward to closing this before year-end.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Marketplace Partnerships
Redwood Inference
